[{"id": "2WkkmVb4j3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🪙Finances Manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "HmQtt1P2vd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Finances module keeps the records of the church's money. It records the gifts that come in, in the Sunday collection or online, and the money that goes out as expenses and help for people in need. It keeps a balance for each fund, gives each giver a yearly statement, and tracks pledges and budgets. Churchit is not full accounting software: when your church also uses one, export a journal to it (see Export to your accounting system).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bfQ6QVMNeu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Church Finance users (the Church Treasurer role profile) and Church Managers work in this module. Only they submit and cancel collections and expenses. Only Church Managers and System Managers change Giving Settings. Other staff do not see gifts. Members give online on the Give page, and see their own pledges and giving statements in the member portal.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ohgbqal-Hz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Finances workspace starts with the work that waits for you, the oldest first: Gifts with No Person (paid online gifts that no person is linked to), Donations Needing Review (online gifts whose charge does not agree with the gift), Pending Expenses (expenses that are saved but not submitted) and Pending Alms Requests (requests that wait for a decision, or approved requests that wait for their expense).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "7IpKXpY84O", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Under them, charts show weekly giving, giving by fund, expenses and the budget summary. The sidebar lists Collections, Online Donations, Expenses, Funds, Pledges and Alms Requests. The reports are in the Giving, Fund Activity, Expenses & Budgets and Accounting folders. Giving Settings, Payment Types, Expense Types and Data Imports are in the Setup folder.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "JrX4QoaprF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🧮How Money Records Work", "col": 12}}, {"id": "NnzX_ljEZL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Collections, expenses and fund transfers go through three states:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hf7TFvz6bm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Draft: you saved it, but it is not final. You can still change it. A draft does not change any fund balance, report or statement.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5p-0aYN6Jv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Submitted: you clicked Submit. It is final and counts in the funds, the reports and the giving statements. You cannot change it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "N0Zm3SDUrj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Cancelled: you clicked Cancel on a submitted record. It stays for your history but no longer counts. To correct it, click Amend: Churchit makes a new draft copy that you fix and submit. You cannot amend the collection of an online gift (see Record a refund).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "L62kIzP0Zv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "So enter the gifts, check them, and submit only when the totals are right.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fKMTWf-J0m", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Good to know", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3esvMI9iDb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When you submit or cancel a collection, an expense or a fund transfer, a short message tells how much each fund changed. When money goes out of a fund and its balance goes below zero, the message gives the new balance.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5TU6MnwAZ_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When you save one of them with a date more than 30 days after today, or more than one year before today, an orange message asks you to check the date. Churchit still saves it, so you can enter old records.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8soe6hCC8q", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- You cannot rename a collection, an expense, a fund transfer or a giving statement. Its ID stays the same as the ID on the printed paper.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "eM7EcKKHMD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Reports for a date range include all of the last day, so a gift at 11:59 PM on the last day counts.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "I8fDDrbQ2Y", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "💵Collections", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2e_40VmQkZ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Collection is the money that the church received at one service or event (a Function), such as the Sunday offering. It holds one row for each gift: a donation. Each donation says who gave, how much, to which fund and how.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "sdmFCydxUk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
After the Sunday service, two counters open a new Collection for Sunday Worship. They type the expected total of the deposit, then enter each envelope: the giver, the amount, the fund and Cash or Check. When the donations add up to the expected total, the collection shows Ready to Submit. The treasurer checks it and clicks Submit. The gifts now count in the fund balances and on each giver's statement.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "6NZjLvsG7d", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Count a collection", "col": 12}}, {"id": "cfYHk6ujCW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Collections and click Add Collection.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "sr1b4IjNOX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Choose the Function where you took the collection. Today's services are at the top of the list. Churchit sets the Date to the day and time of that service. Keep the date of the day the gifts were received, also when you enter the collection days later: giving statements count each gift by this date.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "zLsugb3N-M", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Count the money and type the total in Expected Total, for example the total of the deposit slip.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "N5G1ffw_qY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Add a row in Donations for each gift (see below). Imbalance shows the difference between the donations and the Expected Total.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gEql9vop0a", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "5. Save. A draft shows Unbalanced while its donations do not add up to the Expected Total, and Ready to Submit when they do.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "NYNCnV0h8H", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "6. Check the collection and click Submit. Churchit refuses to submit a collection that has an imbalance: find the missing or wrong gift first.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "6FvLtojj6R", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Linking each collection to its Function lets you later compare the giving of each kind of service.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "WCiulTgupj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Enter donations", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Mz68Sm6cQY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each donation row has Person, Amount, Fund, Check # and Payment Type.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "JGqpET_lpH", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- In Person, type a name or an envelope number to find the giver. Link every gift that you can to a person: only linked gifts are on giving statements and personal reports. A gift with the Payment Type Check must have a Person and a Check #.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A3t25Zeb_G", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Press Tab to move to the next column. Tab in Payment Type adds a new row. A new row starts with the fund and the payment type of the row above it. The first row uses the Default Fund of Giving Settings.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "IzCoqV8u7d", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When one check is for two funds, enter it as two donations, one for each fund, with the same check number.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "LXxKf0ZSLX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Open a row to see its Notes, under More.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kHPN4Z-SjJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The totals of the collection, of each fund and of each payment type update as you type.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "osTbd6KBZO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Envelope numbers. A person can have an Envelope Number: the number on their offering envelopes, or the reference on their bank transfers. Type it in the Person field to find the giver. Two people in one church cannot have the same number. A signed-in member sees their envelope number on the Give page as the reference to use.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "uLPBbcnde6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Non-cash gifts", "col": 12}}, {"id": "CvhNSIj5hb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When someone gives property, such as equipment or food, and not money, add a donation row with the Payment Type Non-Cash. Churchit sets the amount to 0 and opens the row: type what was given in Description.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "RAozLOd0z7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The church describes the gift and does not put a value on it, so a non-cash row cannot have an amount. The giver's statement shows the description in place of an amount. Non-cash gifts do not change fund balances, collection totals or the giving reports. You can mark another Payment Type as non-cash on its form.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "N1jWOoQSls", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Payment types. Churchit starts with Cash, Check, Online and Non-Cash, and you can add your own. Do not rename Check or Online: Churchit asks for a check number on Check, and records every online gift as Online.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ThxQBaWTqN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Print and reconcile", "col": 12}}, {"id": "nw1WWlxBz6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Print (Ctrl+P) opens the Collection Count Sheet: the cash, check and other amount of each fund, with the totals, and a list of the non-cash gifts.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "H1eEV9c5wd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- After you save, click View, then Bank Reconciliation Report, to compare the collection with the bank deposit slip. It lists each check on its own line (a check split across funds stays one line), and the cash and other money as one line for each payment type and fund. It leaves out non-cash gifts, because they do not go to the bank. It works for a draft or a submitted collection, not a cancelled one.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "LWz5dznKum", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Thank-you emails", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5kCnjqazLW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To email a receipt to each giver when a collection is submitted, tick Email Receipts on the Messages tab of Giving Settings. Each giver with an email address gets one email with their amount. It is off on a new site, and a submitted collection then shows a note that givers get no receipt.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "MfPV4Wurqp", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Online gifts send their own receipt. Imported collections send none. The email uses the Email Template Donation Acknowledgment. If you made your own copy of the Donation Acknowledgment notification earlier, turn that copy off when you turn this setting on, or givers get two emails.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wCcz1EonqV", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Giving reports", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Y9CbtVJV-M", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The giving reports are in the Giving folder of the sidebar. They count only submitted collections.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ky9hJh-5FD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Donations: each gift in a date range (this month at first), with filters for fund, payment type and person, and a total.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "yDxWoz58Lb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Donations by Person and Person Donations: the gifts of each person, or of one person, in a date range.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "UmKuE8XW-U", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- YTD Giving by Person: each giver's total this year, the number of gifts, the average gift and last year's total. A check split across funds counts as one gift, and so do the cash gifts of one person in one collection.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "FPY9C1l2fn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- First-Time Givers: the people whose first gift of money was in the last 90 days. Change Window (Days) to look further back.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fkNQBubyVG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Lapsed Givers: the people whose last gift was more than 90 days ago but within the last year, with when they last attended. People who have died are left out. Use it to notice someone who may need a call.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Bf1r3tSyS3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Bank Reconciliation: see above.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_KvqgnlX-2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Non-cash gifts do not count as gifts in these reports or in the Givers number of Weekly Metrics.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Dva8ibyKst", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On the Person form, First Gift, Last Gift and Lapsed Giver come from the submitted collections. Only Church Finance, Church Manager and System Manager users see these fields. A Church Manager can have the Lapsed Givers list emailed to a finance user: click ..., then Setup Auto Email.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "74YC6QVhW0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "💳Online giving", "col": 12}}, {"id": "t0v3leOG7C", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Members and guests can give online on your website's Give page, with a card or PayPal. Each gift goes straight into the fund that the giver chooses, and Churchit records it in a collection by itself.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "cNEAxz6FAn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Online giving needs the Payments app, a separate free Frappe app that Churchit does not install. Until a System Manager installs it, online giving, sign-up payments and form payments are off, and Giving Settings shows a notice. The Churchit README tells how to install it on Frappe Cloud, with Docker or on your own server.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "335FyNSq6B", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Set it up", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lCIklMQ6SL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. A System Manager installs the Payments app on the site.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mKPbkjnVYr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. A System Manager enters the account keys in Stripe Settings or PayPal Settings. Only a System Manager can see and change these keys.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "LtBO9Se7ND", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Open Giving Settings. On the Online Giving tab, add the gateway in Payment Gateways, mark one row as the default, and tick Enable Online Giving.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "iLkVfACbLR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. On each Fund that people may give to, tick Allow giving to this fund.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "jyqMPM387I", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "5. Check the Currency in Giving Settings. When it is empty, Churchit uses the site currency.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9djg1bcMP4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Give link shows in the website menu and footer only while online giving is on.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9R7WZviXOG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Other settings on the Online Giving and Messages tabs:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-uem1KbXUQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Allow Anonymous (Guest) Giving: on at first, so guests can give without a login. When you turn it off, a guest must sign in first, and each gift is linked to a person.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "CV4XkyUdHp", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Default Fund: the fund that the Give page chooses first, and the first fund of a new donation row.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pyLc_Umwwg", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Thank You Message: what the giver sees after a gift. The giver also gets a receipt by email, from the Email Template Donation Acknowledgment.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "T_N9WTMdja", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Choose a gateway. Churchit works with Stripe and PayPal.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Rlv9ZAIxFs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Stripe cannot ask for 3-D Secure, the check in which the bank asks the card holder to confirm a payment. A card that needs it is declined. Many cards in the UK and the EU need it, so churches there use PayPal.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "d8ZZgKo0lg", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- PayPal Settings holds one PayPal account for the whole site. Stripe can hold one account for each church: add one Stripe Settings record for each account.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "52JoOdEnZZ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The payment page shows the card fields of the gateway inside a page of your site. So the card industry's rules (PCI DSS 4.0) for scripts on payment pages apply to your site. Ask your payment processor what it needs from you.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "W4gojrzadZ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "How online gifts are recorded", "col": 12}}, {"id": "VfFH8sf-yi", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When the gateway confirms a payment, Churchit compares what the gateway charged with the Online Donation:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "IICPLrmJ7c", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When they agree, Churchit records the gift in a collection and sets the status to Paid.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "vK6_zZUs9J", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When they do not agree, Churchit records nothing and sets the status to Needs Review. The Church Finance users of the church get a desk alert with both amounts. Check the payment in the gateway before you do anything else.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "V102im-OtO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When the gateway says that the payment did not go through, the status is Failed, and nothing is recorded.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "yZwMdDZ724", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When the gateway charged a gift but the gift stays Pending, for example because the confirmation did not arrive, the Church Finance users get an alert each day. A Church Finance user opens the gift and clicks Record Charged Gift. Churchit checks the payment again and records the gift once.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-pVgeYjny4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Tip
To find a gift from its payment record, type the reference in the Transaction Reference filter of the Online Donations list.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kYLj4cdsTy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Gifts from guests", "col": 12}}, {"id": "igLSg9gkFR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A guest who gives without signing in has no person on the gift, so the gift is not on a giving statement. Click Gifts with No Person on the workspace to find these gifts. Open the Online Donation, set Person and save. The donation row in the collection then names that person, and a comment on the collection says which gift changed. The next giving statement for that year includes the gift. Only Church Finance and Church Manager users can do this.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "NopDVx4ZCB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Processing fees", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qa587-s8nU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A giver can add the processing fee to their gift, so that the church gets the full amount. In the gateway row of Giving Settings, tick Offer Fee Cover and type the card rate in Fee Percent and Fixed Fee, for example 2.9 and 0.30.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Qqg3ekebKH", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Give page then offers Cover the processing fee with the amount. Churchit works out the fee itself, so the giver cannot change it. The fee is part of the gift: the Online Donation shows it in Covered Fee, and the collection, the receipt and the statement show the full payment.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "O3U5uDSuZq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Give links and QR codes", "col": 12}}, {"id": "unmGyDl3XR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Open a Fund that takes online gifts and click Give Link. A window shows a QR code and the address of the Give page with this fund chosen.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-IzDMyHpTg", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Download QR Code gives the code as a picture for a bulletin, a poster or a giving card.
- Copy Link copies the address. To fill in an amount, add &amount=25 to the end.
- To make a tap-to-give tag, write the address on an NFC tag with a phone app.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "BTEVvH0R4h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
For the building campaign, the treasurer opens the Building Fund, clicks Give Link and downloads the QR code. The bulletin prints it with \"Scan to give to the new roof\". Each scan opens the Give page with the Building Fund chosen.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XKqNsxikd1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Text-to-give", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mSpe4S9ioA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "With text-to-give, a person sends a text to a phone number and gets back a link to the Give page. Churchit does not receive texts, so your text provider sends this reply.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "IEGX1lXPA6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Get a separate phone number for giving from your text provider, such as Twilio. Do not use the number that sends your Church Emails, because the reply goes to every text that comes in.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "TP_vqPW4fA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Get the link: your site address followed by /give, for example https://yourchurch.org/give, or a fund's Give Link.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "e4zCMqAE0k", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Set the number to reply with the link. In Twilio, add a TwiML Bin with this text and your link: <Response><Message>Thank you for giving. Give here: https://yourchurch.org/give</Message></Response>. Write each & in the link as &. Then open the phone number in Twilio, choose this bin under A message comes in, and save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "sqXdqJSdWY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Send a text to the number from your own phone, and make sure that the link comes back and opens the Give page.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kA-p6Pi4jt", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit does not log these texts. STOP replies work as for all texts (see Text replies and STOP in the Communications manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "yIL_rw06bh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Other ways to give", "col": 12}}, {"id": "HDASaEv0XY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Write your bank transfer, standing order or mail details in Other Ways to Give on the Messages tab of Giving Settings. The Give page shows this text below the form. When online giving is off, the page shows only this text, with a note that online giving is not available. Enter these gifts in a collection as usual.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "DmSogYHG8D", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Record a refund", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YYv37L5W24", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Refund the gift at the payment processor first. Churchit does not send money back.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "93lkHkOC49", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- For a full refund in the same year as the gift, open the gift's collection and cancel it. Churchit takes the gift out of the fund and sets the Online Donation to Refunded. Do not amend that collection.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "4TKhMfxcma", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- For a partial refund, a refund in a later year, or a gift whose dates you already exported to your accounting system: make a new collection with the date of the refund. Add a donation for the same person and fund with a negative amount, for example -20, and submit it. The statement for the year of the refund shows the lower total.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "SRF4yYafif", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Payments for sign-ups and forms", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qNe-C2LUmf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A function sign-up or a form with a price takes an online payment through the same gateways (see the Ministries manual for prices). Each payment comes in as a submitted collection with one row for the fund of the function or the form, and no person, so it is not on a giving statement.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "jQKOZ9MroI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When the gateway charged a wrong amount, or charged a record that is already paid, Churchit records nothing and alerts the Church Finance users. Each day it also alerts them about payments that a gateway charged but that are not recorded.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "71cqYWmY5T", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "For a sign-up paid in cash or by check, open the sign-up and click Payment, then Record Offline Payment. Churchit makes no collection, so put the money in the weekly collection.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gAFt54FziR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When a paid sign-up is cancelled or declined, or loses its place, its Payment Status is Refund Due and Church Finance gets an alert. Refund it at the payment processor and cancel its collection or add a negative donation, then click Payment, then Record Refund on the sign-up (or Record Refund on the Form Response).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "xlE1FGbCG5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "With more than one church", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ak-qpk6h8t", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each gateway row in Giving Settings has a Church. Name a church and that gateway serves only that church, so each church's gifts reach its own account. Leave it blank and every church can use it. Wording Per Church, on the Messages tab, gives a church its own thank-you message, statement wording and Other Ways to Give. A Give Link names the fund's church, and that church must be published.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "HH7DwOfrZO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🧾Giving statements", "col": 12}}, {"id": "f35kTizV2y", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Giving Statement lists a giver's gifts for a period, usually a year, for their tax records.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "K-TfyQRkzj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Make the statements", "col": 12}}, {"id": "CE8_rq2AQY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Giving Statements and click Generate Statements.
2. Check the From Date and To Date. They start as January 1 to December 31 of last year.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kf3sy4abS9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit makes the statements from the submitted collections in those dates. Run it again at any time: it rebuilds the statements with the latest gifts.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3_elt1963t", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Group Statements By, on the Statements tab of Giving Settings, makes one statement for each household (at first) or one for each person. A household statement is addressed to its primary contact. If the primary contact changes, or you change this setting, run Generate Statements again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "DmnZR0s6Sk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When no gift in those dates is linked to a person, Generate Statements makes no statement and says so.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3a6bKHK3Jo", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A statement shows only gifts to funds that have Tax Deductible ticked (see Funds).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ODSaZWMads", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A non-cash gift shows its description in place of an amount, and the total counts only money.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "WSE0l_m2xT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Generate Statements never removes a statement that you made by hand, a statement that was emailed, or a statement of another church. When a rebuild changes a statement that was emailed, it shows Not Sent again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "EQWFIQrN2z", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Members see their own statements, and their household's, on the Giving Statements page of the member portal, where they can open and print them. So a statement is visible to the giver as soon as you generate it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "TI4Qdep9rl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Print opens the Contribution Statement, with the household name and mailing address.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "s7eCCQsG_0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Email the statements", "col": 12}}, {"id": "CiEqfW3rNk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. In the Giving Statements list, click Email Statements.
2. Enter the same From Date and To Date, and click Email.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "83wH4z3s-6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit sends each statement as a PDF to the giver's primary email, in the background. It tells you how many will be emailed, how many have no email address and how many were already emailed. The list shows each statement as Emailed, Not Sent or No Email.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fAEWCjfOvg", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Print and mail the statements that have no email address. If the site cannot send email yet, a System Manager must set up outgoing email: you can still print every statement from the list.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "GSkfl3lr45", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A giver who unsubscribed from all email gets no statement email.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QroDpdvXuw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A statement is emailed only once. If a gift changes and you generate the statements again, the next Email Statements sends the new statement. To send all of them again, tick Send again to statements already emailed.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "InVeytujUz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- To change the text of the email, edit the Email Template Giving Statement.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lYKYTlWxRJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
In January, the treasurer generates the statements for last year and checks a few of them. She clicks Email Statements: 180 go by email and 25 have no email address. She prints those 25 and mails them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-E5SeLq1FI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "With more than one church, a statement is issued by the church that received the gifts. A giver who gave at two churches gets a statement from each.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Sro9AQ9sHU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📥Import giving history", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5lRn4XVnVA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "You can add past gifts from another church system, a spreadsheet or your payment processor. Church Finance users, Church Managers and System Managers can import gifts. Each row of the file is one gift. Churchit puts the gifts of one batch on one date in one draft collection. Check each draft collection and submit it. The gifts count only after you submit. Churchit sends no thank-you email for imported gifts.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "WNzygmW_UN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The file", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5bvEEi2fyn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "You must fill in Gift ID, Date, Amount, Fund and Payment Type.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "W4ZhI_vmaK", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Gift ID: the ID of the gift in the old system, for example a Stripe charge ID. Churchit imports each gift only once.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tB4OrbBs96", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Date and Amount: the date and the full amount that the giver paid.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "KtP0ML2tZ5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Fund and Payment Type: a fund and a payment type of your church. A Check also needs a Check Number.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0jskF_c8n3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Imported From and Person ID: the system name and the giver's ID from your People import. Leave Imported From blank when you imported the people from a spreadsheet.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9gSe3105bA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Email: finds the giver when the Person ID does not.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "jkpxGLO74a", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Batch: the gifts of one batch and one date go in one collection. Blank uses the name of the import.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "MTi_hhyFMD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Notes: text for the donation.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "aRjiK_Wt9c", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Import it", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3N2P3H2-x1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. In the Setup folder of the sidebar, click Data Imports, then Add Data Import. Set Document Type to Giving Import and keep Insert New Records.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lUnSiyLLcl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Save, and click Download Template to get the columns.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_zCw4nBtQM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Upload your file and click Next. Match any column that Churchit does not know, or leave it out.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3JiIq4npD3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Look at the preview. Correct the rows that cannot be imported, or click Skip Row.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_oTqvBd3pt", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "5. Click Import. Then open Collections, filter on Import Batch, check each draft collection and submit it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "4B0sq8kBr3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The preview stops a row when Churchit does not know its fund or payment type, when no person or more than one person has its Person ID or email, when its Gift ID is already in Churchit or earlier in the file, when its payment type is non-cash, or when an online gift with the same amount, date and email is already in Churchit. So a second import of the same file adds nothing.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QY66k5FORb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The preview also stops a row whose fund belongs to another church. A gift whose collection was cancelled can be imported again. When the matching online gift is Pending or Needs Review, record it from the Online Donation, not from the import.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_7zEllncgr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If your church made its own copy of the Donation Acknowledgment notification, set its Condition to doc.donations and not doc.import_batch before you submit imported collections. Otherwise each giver gets an email for each old gift.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "S4nhiXRyjw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Import gifts from Stripe", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XWi-oNURu3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Use this for gifts that givers made on Stripe's own pages, such as recurring gifts. Churchit already has the gifts from your Give page.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qFksBXviHF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. In the Stripe Dashboard, open Payments, set the dates and click Export.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "06TVcFppdv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Open the file in a spreadsheet. Delete each row whose Description starts with \"Online gift to the\" (gifts from your Give page), each row whose Status is not Paid, and each row with an Amount Refunded.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "U2RXyzJjit", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Rename the columns id to Gift ID, Created date (UTC) to Date and Customer Email to Email. Keep Amount and delete the other columns.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "PoXAa1Tsv_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Add the columns Fund and Payment Type, and fill them in on each row. You can add a Batch column, for example with the month.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "7Myg-NmZV5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "5. Import the file as above. Stripe gives the date in UTC, so a gift late in the evening can have the next day's date.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "W6a7yShLd0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📊Funds", "col": 12}}, {"id": "PddPOdPpnU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Fund is a pot of money for one purpose, such as General, Building or Missions. Every gift goes into a fund, and every expense comes out of one. Churchit keeps the Balance of each fund from these records, so you cannot type it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3S9ABM5Zel", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
The church raises money for a new roof. You add a Building Fund with a Goal Amount of $40,000, tick Allow giving to this fund and print its QR code. Gifts in collections and online go into it, the Goal Progress shows how far you are, and the roofing invoice is an expense from the same fund.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "nkVPtFXUd6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The Ledger tab lists every transaction of the fund: the gifts, the expenses and the fund transfers. A gift takes the date of its collection.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YQh46GZeEQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The Fundraising Goal section holds a Goal Amount, the Goal Progress and the start and end dates.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "xbU3b7fLF_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Allow giving to this fund puts the fund on the Give page.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "42LaVN6Ohi", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Two funds of one church cannot have the same name.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "K28Oq85cez", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Do not type rows in the Ledger by hand: the balance follows the rows. Use a fund transfer or an expense instead.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Dg-DSaLoQn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Move money between funds", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_MCvq9Vm_v", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To move money from one fund to another, add a Fund Transfer and submit it. Churchit adds a transaction to each fund, such as \"Transfer to Building\". When a transfer would take the From Fund below zero, Churchit warns you when you save it. To record money that is spent, add an Expense instead.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "NANe1ZKsWG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Tax Deductible", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pRr0mWaMd5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Giving statements are tax receipts, so they show only gifts to funds that have Tax Deductible ticked. New funds have it ticked. Untick it for a fund whose gifts are not tax deductible, for example a collection that you pass on to another organization.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YOpkTAnyuG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Fund reports", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0JAkb4ExrA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The fund reports are in the Fund Activity folder: Fund Balances, Fund Transactions, Transactions by Date, Fund Goals (the funds with a goal, with what is left to raise) and the Fund Goals Dashboard, which shows the balance of each fund and the progress toward each goal.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8Ih-qBJJk4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Income Statement, in the Accounting folder, shows the income, the expenses and the net of each fund, for the last 12 months at first. The transaction reports name the record behind each row: a Collection, an Expense or a Fund Transfer.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "p49WN89hYY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Funds with more than one church", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tuDQCAcHCu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A fund belongs to one church until you tick Shared with All Churches on it. Then every church can give to it and spend from it, for example a joint building fund. Its balance and its transactions are the joint ones.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "jp_QBGC_BA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each gift and expense still belongs to the church that gave or spent it, so the reports show each church only its own money. Only the church that shared a fund can stop sharing it, and only the church that owns a fund can move its money with a transfer.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "jJaZCuACbY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🙏Pledges", "col": 12}}, {"id": "h8waup2nP9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A pledge is a promise to give a total amount to a campaign, such as $1,200 to the building campaign over a year. Churchit follows how much of each pledge has come in.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "baDwa-SQy5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
The church starts a building campaign for one year, with the Building Fund. The Smith family pledges $1,200. Each month they give $100 to the Building Fund, in the collection or online. The Pledge Progress report shows their $1,200 pledged, the amount given so far and the amount still to give.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "HYKS99YK3O", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Start a campaign", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Gl3E-TSCCz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Add a Pledge Campaign with a title, the fund that receives its gifts, a start date, an end date and, if you want, a goal amount. Each campaign belongs to your church. On a saved campaign, click View, then Pledge Progress, to see its report.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "P4uhExxj7T", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Record a pledge", "col": 12}}, {"id": "uDGcSAIzj9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Add a Pledge with the person, the campaign and the pledged amount. Frequency records how often the giver plans to give, and does not change the amount.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "EEDzDp02di", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Set Family to make it a household pledge: the gifts of everyone in the household then count, and each adult of the household can see it in the member portal.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "JR-WL6dLE6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When one person has two pledges to one campaign, their gifts fill the older pledge first.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "TLcWT1oTXl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Pledges in the member portal", "col": 12}}, {"id": "enAPdtSWNR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Members pledge on the Pledges page of the member portal. A member clicks Make a pledge, chooses a campaign of their church that has not ended, and types the amount and how often they plan to give. The page lists the member's pledges, also the ones that staff entered from a pledge card, with the amount given and the amount still to give.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "q92CHyLDLL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A member can change a pledge that they made while its campaign is open, but not a pledge that staff added. While the church takes gifts online, each pledge has a Give toward this pledge button that opens the Give page with the campaign's fund chosen.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "NGSuWCHViE", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Pledge Progress", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mR8zQvhjVQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Pledge Progress report shows each campaign with its goal, the total pledged and the total received, then each pledge with the amount received from its giver. A gift counts when its collection is submitted, it goes to the campaign's fund, its collection belongs to the campaign's church, and its date is in the campaign's dates. Enter each gift in a collection as usual: there is no separate pledge payment.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "EPU3LABtxn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "💸Expenses", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9WI_98iVpm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "An Expense records money that the church pays out, such as a utility bill, a missionary's support or a repair. Each expense has an Expense Type, and the expense type names the fund that pays it. When you submit the expense, the money comes out of that fund.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qr6IvSkdKn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Add an expense", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kiQ1rOPq2W", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Expenses and click Add Expense.
2. Fill in the Date, the Amount (more than 0), the Vendor and the Type. The vendor's Default Expense Type fills Type for you.
3. Save. The expense is Pending until someone submits it.
4. Click Print to get the Expense Voucher, a check request with lines for signatures.
5. Click Submit when the expense is approved.
6. After you pay it, fill in Paid On and Payment Reference, such as the check number.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XpBsWClrwd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When an expense would take its fund below zero, a saved expense shows an orange note with the balance that the fund would have, so the person who submits it sees it first. To undo an expense, cancel it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kbQXB0kpOo", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Good to know", "col": 12}}, {"id": "HyQglWTve-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Choose a Ministry on an expense to add it to that ministry's Total Expenses when you submit it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "TMdxAGftVP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Churchit makes a draft expense each day for each missionary support payment that is due, when the missionary has Auto-create Expenses on (see the Missions manual). These drafts show the Missionary. Check and submit them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YoCuiFh31U", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Churchit has no approval step for expenses apart from Submit. To email the Church Managers about each new expense, a System Manager turns on a copy of the Expense Pending Approval notification (see Notifications in the Communications manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "H8yeEbdzfC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Expense types", "col": 12}}, {"id": "uPWIu9A1TP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Expense Types sort your expenses for reports, such as Utilities or Office Supplies. Each expense type names the fund that pays it. Expense types can be grouped: tick Is Group on Utilities, then choose Utilities as the Parent Expense Type of Electricity and Water. The Expenses report then shows the types under a group when you choose the group.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "x3dpMYIkrs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Expense types are shared by every church, but the fund that one names may not be. If a branch is told that the fund belongs to another church, share that fund, or give the branch an expense type of its own with a fund it can use.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mg6x7wKUY0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Suggest Type with AI", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lHnj_854xX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When AI is turned on (see the Foundations manual), Church Finance and Church Manager users see Suggest Type on a new or draft expense. The AI reads the notes of the expense, the vendor's name when the vendor has Is a Business ticked, and the names of your expense types. It never gets the amount, the fund or bank details. Click Use This Type to fill Type, then save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0dFzEp7RDn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Tick Is a Business on each vendor that is a company, shop or organization: the name of a vendor who is a person is never sent. A vendor whose name or email matches a person in your directory counts as a person, even with Is a Business ticked. Suggest Type does not show on an expense made for a missionary, because the Missionary sets its type.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "38AN9ahl_i", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🫴Alms", "col": 12}}, {"id": "yn3wpuCVwl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Alms are money that the church gives to someone in need, such as help with rent or groceries. An Alms Request records the need, the decision and the payment. (For money given to the church, see Collections.)", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lPxuiE85KN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
A member asks for help with an electric bill of $180. The care team adds an alms request for the family, and approves it after a visit. The treasurer gets an email, writes the check and clicks Create Expense. The money comes out of the benevolence fund, and the request shows Distributed.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "LO5NrwBcTc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Handle a request", "col": 12}}, {"id": "K2eTOIM97N", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Add an Alms Request with the Recipient (a person or a family), the Amount and the need. With more than one church, the Requester must be a person of your church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2cs1ycp6nn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. The care team sets the Status to Approved or Declined.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mrymkQBzHN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. When the money is paid, click Actions, then Create Expense. Pick an Expense Type if the request has none. Churchit makes and submits the Expense, takes the money out of the fund, and sets the request to Distributed. If you set the status to Distributed yourself, Churchit asks whether to record the expense now.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "g1fmaSGtep", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Good to know", "col": 12}}, {"id": "y9x2BIGfYP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Each request gets one expense. If you cancel that expense, the request goes back to Approved. To pay it again, amend the cancelled expense and submit it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "JOdkl6cxAx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- You cannot delete a request while its expense is submitted. Cancel the expense first.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "JT_fmBU5ue", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When someone adds an alms request, the Church Pastoral Care users and the Church Managers of its church get an email and a desk notification (New Alms Request). When a request is approved, the Church Finance users get one (Alms Request Approved) so that they pay it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9qK-sM3VQB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Requests from members", "col": 12}}, {"id": "V-P-7NDbnq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Members ask for help on the Benevolence Requests page of the member portal. They click Ask for help, choose who the help is for, and type the amount and the need. The page lists their requests with the status. A member can change or delete a request only while it is Pending, and can add a comment that the care team sees.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "uJGhKprozm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Case notes", "col": 12}}, {"id": "o8WEB5SWxO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On a saved alms request, click View, then Case Notes, to read the notes about the person who gets the alms. Click Actions, then Add Case Note, to add a note in the Benevolence category. For a Family, the notes go on its primary contact, or on the Requester when the family has none. Only the Pastoral Care team and the Church Managers can read Benevolence notes. The finance team does not see them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Hk9qy4xvOB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📊Budgets", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-KRd_vRsGw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Budget says how much the church plans to spend on each expense type in a period, usually a year. Churchit then compares the plan with what you actually spent.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "FvQn_XyYkn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Add a Budget with the start and end dates.
2. Add a row in Expense Lines for each expense type, with the budgeted amount and notes if you want. Add All Expense Types under the table adds a row for each type. The Total Budgeted adds itself up.
3. Save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "cAqlyqT6Ry", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "An expense type can be in a budget only once. Churchit warns you when a budget has a group type and one of its sub-types (their spending would count twice), and when its dates overlap another budget. The Status part of the form shows the total spent, the percent used and what remains.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0q5ciUuxlz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Click View, then Budget vs Actual, to compare the budget with the submitted expenses of each type. It also shows what you expected to spend by today, the draft expenses that wait, and whether each type is over or under budget.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "x6IllPCbrn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Choose a comparison, such as the same period last year, to see the spending of an earlier time beside it. The Budget Summary chart on the Finances workspace shows the same comparison. With more than one church, each church can have its own budget for the same dates, and Include Branch Churches adds the spending of the branches.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_ooywQ4n5l", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
The budget for this year gives Utilities $6,000. In June, Budget vs Actual shows $3,400 spent on Utilities: 57% used at the middle of the year, so the church is a little over plan.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_9akbs2xRm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🏪Vendors", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YbiCi3La2V", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Vendor is a company or person that the church pays, such as the electric company or a plumber.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "v8CIxVX4EY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Add Vendor opens a short form for the name, the Default Expense Type, the phone and the email. Click Edit Full Form for the address and notes.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "IpmzP9ilZR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The Default Expense Type fills in Type when you choose the vendor on an expense.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "vzOrhHwVo9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Tick Is a Business for a company, shop or organization (see Suggest Type with AI).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kjW-vjEhKK", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Untick Active on a vendor that you no longer use. Do not delete it: its past expenses keep their link, and new expenses do not offer it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "R4G2DX-wLs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A vendor's expenses are in the Connections section of its form.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "SjGRbKNpno", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📒Export to your accounting system", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wg-vrumvCS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit keeps its own fund ledger. If your church also uses an accounting system, such as QuickBooks, you can send it a journal of the gifts, expenses and fund transfers.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "knhEbeoNle", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open GL Account Mappings and add one mapping for each record. Mapping For says what the record is, Record is the fund, payment type, expense type or church, and Account is the account exactly as your accounting system shows it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "R6Cs2IXk07", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Map each fund to the account its money goes to, each payment type (Cash, Check, Card) to the account the money comes into, each expense type to its expense account, and your church to the account that pays expenses.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ULtvh7NQKg", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3.
